solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Though in favour of an acceptable offer, say no

parts.note: surface padding: it sets up the contrast in the story and gives no letters
to be for something is to favour it
a bid is an offer made in the hope it is accepted

explanation.surface: Someone likes a generous offer yet still turns it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes "say no" a response to the offer, but it is the definition on its own, and "Though" is only there for the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to prohibit something is to say no to it.

clue.text: Remit fee for no-working period

indicators.note: to remit is also to send back or alter, so the letters of REMIT and FEE are sent back rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: An employer waives a charge in exchange for a spell off work.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is thin: the two words simply rearrange, and "remit" doubles as the only hint of change.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hours off, when you are not at work, are a no-working period.

clue.text: Very hungry creature that flies round the States

parts.note: a raven is a bird, the creature that flies

explanation.surface: A starving bird circles over America.
explanation.walkthrough: "Round" looks like an instruction to put one thing around another; it is just the letter O, and the pieces join in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: starving, greedy for food, is very hungry.

clue.text: It's on the cards it might precede crisis

definitions.meaning: not "likely": the word printed on a card that proves who you are
the word that comes before crisis in a phrase for doubting who you are

explanation.walkthrough: "On the cards" is an idiom for "likely", but here it is literal: the thing written on ID cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are phrase completions: ID means identity on a card, and an identity crisis is doubt about oneself.

clue.text: Debit one transferred, following orders

indicators.note: the letters are moved to new positions, as money is transferred between accounts

explanation.surface: A bank clerk moves a single debit exactly as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: The banking words "debit" and "transferred" make the surface look financial; the debit is really just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective phrase for an adjective: compliant, doing as told.

clue.text: A member of the fair sex

definitions.text: A member of the fair sex

parts.note: the old phrase for women, but read "fair" as light-haired

explanation.walkthrough: "The fair sex" is an old phrase for women, but here "fair" means fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on fair: a woman with light hair belongs to the fair sex twice over.

clue.text: Element of risk in garden design

indicators.note: a design arranges things, so the letters of GARDEN are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A landscape plan includes a hazardous feature.
explanation.walkthrough: "Design" sits in the garden surface as landscaping; it tells you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: peril, the chance of harm, is an element of risk.

clue.text: Creator of a well-known tour of Paris

definitions.text: Creator of a well-known tour of Paris

parts.note: not a sightseeing trip: tour is French for tower

explanation.walkthrough: "Tour" reads as a sightseeing trip, but it is French for tower: the answer is the engineer behind the Tour Eiffel.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: Gustave Eiffel's firm designed and built Paris's famous iron tower.

clue.text: Set to work with new tutor after assembly

indicators.note: the letters are put together again, as parts are in an assembly

parts.note: N is the usual abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Pupils get down to work with a new teacher once school assembly is over.
explanation.walkthrough: "Assembly" looks like the school gathering; it signals the letters being put back together.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: to get down to a job is to set to work.

clue.text: Begrudged having to compete in the final round

indicators.note: the contest word is put in the word for the finish

parts.note: the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A player resents being made to play in the last round.
explanation.walkthrough: "The final round" suggests a sports stage, but it just means the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A past-tense synonym: to have resented another's good fortune is to have begrudged it.

clue.text: Being in favour of making an attack

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase has two senses: liking something, and lunging at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Two idioms: you can favour an idea by choosing it, or set upon a person physically.

clue.text: A number set about forming principles

indicators.note: letters knocked about are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A group of people sets about drawing up a list of principles.
explanation.walkthrough: "A number" is the vague crossword pointer to any number word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: beliefs held as true are principles.

clue.text: Disciple has to stick to holy writ

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, part of holy scripture

explanation.surface: A follower must keep faithfully to scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one religious instruction; "has" is only a link, and "to stick" is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a follower of a leader or creed is a disciple.

clue.text: Frightened, a student is ready to fight

parts.note: L for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A scared student nonetheless gears up for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first, set off by the comma; the rest builds the word left to right.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: startled and afraid is frightened.

clue.text: A pound note gets you a drink

parts.note: L is the sign for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A one-pound banknote is enough to buy you a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: "A pound note" reads as a banknote, but it splits into three pieces: A, a pound, a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: beer of this kind is one example of a drink.

clue.text: Bay horses

parts.note: a reddish-brown colour of horse, not a stretch of coast

explanation.walkthrough: "Bay" invites a colour word or a coastline; it only describes the horses, and the answer is their general name as things ridden.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a bay horse under saddle is one kind of riding animal.

clue.text: Litter depositary?

parts.note: not rubbish, but a litter of piglets
the place where they are kept

explanation.walkthrough: "Litter" suggests rubbish and a bin; it is a litter of piglets and their pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on litter: a pigpen is where a sow's young are kept.

clue.text: Prize piece of china?

explanation.walkthrough: "Piece of china" hints at a country; it is crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a trophy awarded as a prize, and a porcelain vessel for tea.

clue.text: Showing unusual maturity, but lacking a certain element

indicators.note: unusual means not in its normal state, so the remaining letters take an unusual order
the word goes without its A

explanation.surface: Someone precociously grown-up turns out to be missing some essential quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The "a" does double duty in the surface: it is the letter dropped, leaving "certain element" as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a rare-earth metal, number 39, is one particular chemical element.

clue.text: Pole shows renewed stamina after Marathon start

indicators.note: the letters of STAMINA are made over in a new form

explanation.surface: A Polish runner gets a second wind after the start of a marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pole" looks like a Polish athlete, which suits the marathon surface; it is a ship's spar.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a sailing ship's principal upright spar is a pole.

clue.text: Guarantee financial asset

explanation.walkthrough: One word, two money senses: a pledge given as guarantee, and a tradable stock or bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: collateral pledged against a loan, and a share or bond traded on markets.

clue.text: Expression of disgust covered by subsequent hilarity

indicators.note: the grunt is covered by the other word, so sits inside it

explanation.surface: Someone's initial disgust is drowned out by the laughs that follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the disgust first, but it ends up in the middle of the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: the sound of amusement is what hilarity produces.

clue.text: She provides father with a cooked meal

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: cooking works a thing into a new form, so MEAL's letters are rearranged

parts.note: surface padding joining father to the meal; no letters

explanation.surface: A woman makes her father a hot dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: "She" is the definition: a woman's name is all it asks for, one of the loosest definitions setters allow.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: any woman's name can stand for "she".

clue.text: Confront with small account charge

parts.note: AC is the short form of account

explanation.surface: A customer is challenged over a minor fee on their bill.
explanation.walkthrough: "Small" tells you to shorten "account" to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to approach and challenge someone boldly is to confront them.

clue.text: Later perhaps, but not too late

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves seem to contradict each other, which is the joke: the phrase means both.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one phrase: eventually, and early enough.

clue.text: Row about batting less

indicators.note: the row goes about the batting word, surrounding it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over reduced batting.
explanation.walkthrough: "Row" reads as a quarrel, which suits the cricket surface, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose comparative synonym: smaller in size is less.

clue.text: Take a chance with the better half

indicators.note: only half of BETTER is kept, the first three of its six letters

explanation.surface: A husband gambles with his wife, his better half.
explanation.walkthrough: "The better half" is a jokey phrase for a spouse; here it means half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to gamble or wager is to take a chance.

clue.text: Worker about to fight — watch out!

indicators.note: the worker goes about the fight word, surrounding it

parts.note: a worker bee; worker is the standard crossword pointer to BEE or ANT

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a labourer is squaring up for a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: "Worker" looks like any labourer; in crosswords it is usually the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are imperatives: a warning to take care is to watch out.

clue.text: Fraudster punished and imprisoned

parts.note: a con man is a fraudster

explanation.surface: A swindler is both fined and jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sentencing report; the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: shut in or locked up is imprisoned.

clue.text: Such heroes are not celebrated

parts.note: points to an adjective that often goes before "heroes"
not praised, and literally no song is made about them

explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase "unsung heroes" names people whose deeds go unpraised; "celebrated" plays on songs of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: heroes nobody praises in song are the ones the phrase describes.

clue.text: First love in a girl is moving

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O

indicators.note: the letters of IN A GIRL move to new places

explanation.surface: A first romance with a girl is an emotional experience.
explanation.walkthrough: "In" looks like a container signal, but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: earliest, the first version of something.

clue.text: A trail that winds, there may be a catch in it

definitions.text: there may be a catch in it

indicators.note: a winding trail twists about, so its letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A twisting path may hide a snag somewhere along it.
explanation.walkthrough: "A catch" reads as a snag, but a lasso's noose catches cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a lasso's loop is where the caught animal ends up.

clue.text: There is nothing amiss in such speculations

indicators.note: amiss means gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone insists there is no harm in speculating.
explanation.walkthrough: "Nothing amiss" reads as "no problem"; in fact O joins the first two words and all of it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: untested ideas and conjectures are speculations.

clue.text: A long-distance runner?

parts.note: a race over a long course, which needs stamina
not only an athlete: in racing, a horse is a runner

explanation.walkthrough: "Runner" suggests an athlete; in horse racing the word for a horse that lasts long races is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing term: a horse that keeps going over long distances is described this way.
